name_reason: Compliant fd2_<domain>_<descriptor>. '4e' is the dispatch-table index 0x4E (entry @ 0x51CC9), a domain ID, not an address residue. Descriptor corrected from '__unref_sentinel' to '__ch29_dragon_down_3': the slot is LIVE, reached via the ch29 kill-drop path -- ch29 char_spawn_record[2] = a defense-core dragon (enemy_data 37, char_id 0x69, lv30) carries pickup_kind=2 param=0x4E, so the dragon's death dispatches consequence[0x4E], setting tile_event_consumed_flags[0x14]=1 to mark this dragon destroyed (one of the ch29 3-dragon objective flags 0x12/0x13/0x14 set by 0x49/0x4D/0x4E). The earlier 'unref' verdict only scanned turn-event/tile-step hooks and missed the kill-drop path.
purpose: Chapter 29 defense-core-dragon progress marker (dispatch slot 0x4E, reached via the ch29 kill-drop path when the dragon record[2] enemy_data 37, pickup_kind=2 param=0x4E, falls): marks this dragon destroyed by setting tile_event_consumed_flags[0x14] = 1 (one of the 3-dragon objective flags), with no other side effects.
logic_summary: Watcom __CHK(4) stack-probe prologue, then a single byte store: *(uint8*)(tile_event_consumed_flags_ptr + 0x14) = 1; return. No branches, no other side effects. Ignores the dispatch arg. Self-contained 10-byte stub (PUSH 4; CALL __CHK; MOV EAX,[flags_ptr]; MOV byte[EAX+0x14],1; RET); no borrowed/hosted tail and nothing tail-JMPs into it (only the data table references it).

params.name: event_arg
params.semantics: Dispatch-table arg under the 1-arg cdecl per-event ABI (table @ 0x51B91). The body does (void)event_arg and never reads it, so it carries no semantic role here.
params.reason: Generic 'event_arg' is the established chevt2.c convention for handlers that ignore the dispatch arg (vs 'stepping_char_id' used by tile-step handlers that consume it). No address residue. Matches sibling handler_4d. (Live Ghidra currently shows 'int stepping_char_id'; that Ghidra-side discrepancy is left for Stage 2 reconciliation -- src convention 'event_arg' is correct for an unread arg.)
